phase6.6f_verdict: REGRESSION. MIMIC i2t R@10 best=3.95% (FAILED gate: < 8.23%). t2i R@10=7.90%. val/clip_loss floor=2.74, total_loss best=2.8404. KD warmup worked (cos_teacher→0.895 at step 1000). No cold-start spike (first clip=2.93, not 3.52). ROOT CAUSE: MoCo queue fills with BiomedCLIP-text-space clustered embeddings (momentum encoder hard-resynced after KD warmup) → queue is full of near-duplicate text negatives → i2t InfoNCE adversarially hard → poor CLIP gradient → i2t collapses. Massive i2t/t2i asymmetry (3.95% vs 7.90%) is diagnostic: t2i uses 32 in-batch image negatives (diverse) while i2t uses 256 clustered text queue negatives. Best checkpoints: step=002717 (2.8438), step=003086 (2.8404 best), step=004229 (2.8423).

key_findings: BiomedCLIP-text KD warmup (α=1.0, 1000 steps) migrates Mamba text to BiomedCLIP text space (cos→0.89) before CLIP engages — improves cross-domain generalisation +0.68pp Indiana vs Phase 5c
img_proj removal (Phase 8): BiomedCLIP visual already outputs 512-d joint embeddings; random-init MLP on top distorted them; removing it improved paired cos 0.226→0.258

MoCo queue post-KD-warmup failure: momentum encoder hard-resynced at unfreeze inherits KD-aligned state → all K queue embeddings cluster in BiomedCLIP-text space → i2t InfoNCE adversarially hard → i2t collapses. Diagnostic: i2t/t2i asymmetry (3.95% vs 7.90% in Phase 6f vs ~8% symmetric in Phase 6e)
K=0 (in-batch, 32 negatives) is strictly better than any K>0 post-warmup, despite 512× smaller pool, because queue negatives are near-duplicates post-KD
Phase 5c (K=16384 warm from step 0, no KD warmup) remains best MIMIC in-distribution (9.99%) but worst Indiana (3.36%). KD warmup is the key differentiator for cross-domain.
